what: Accumulate moderate-intensity aerobic activity (e.g., brisk walking, dancing, cycling) across the week; count every session, including short chunks.
dose: 150-300 min/week moderate OR 75-150 min/week vigorous, or an equivalent combination (WHO 2020; Saudi MOH: at least 150 min moderate or 75 min vigorous, up to 300 min moderate for more benefit). CDC: can be split into smaller chunks, e.g., 30 min x 5 days.
why: WHO states some activity is better than none and more is better; meeting the weekly range provides health benefits for adults.

sources.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
Saudi Ministry of Health - Physical Activity (health awareness)
CDC - Physical activity guidelines for adults
The recommended amount of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration for healthy Saudis: A joint consensus statement of the Saudi Public Health Authority

cue_suggestion: After Asr prayer on her 4 home-workout days; walking fills the other days.
minimum_version: 10 min brisk walk or one dance song block - it still counts toward the weekly total.
normal_version: 30-40 min moderate session (brisk walk or home cardio) on ~4-5 days/week to land in 150-300 min.
bonus_version: Add 1-2 vigorous intervals sessions (e.g., stairs, fast dance) - 1 min vigorous is roughly equal to 2 min moderate in guideline math.
joy_pairing: Pair with a favourite playlist/podcast used only during activity; rotate formats (walk, dance workout, cycling) weekly for novelty.
friction_down: Weekly minutes bar in the app that auto-adds walks and workouts; shoes and mat kept visible; pre-chosen workout video queued the night before.
friction_up_for_competing: Put the phone's entertainment apps behind a 'after movement' shortcut on workout days.
if_then_plan: If it is Asr time on a workout day and I feel low energy, then I will do the 10-minute minimum version instead of skipping.
tracking_metric: Active minutes this week (auto-sum) vs 150 target.
progression: Self-paced: start from current weekly minutes and build toward 150, then toward 300 (sources state the range, not a weekly increase rate).
safety_or_stop_rule: See BODY-25 stop rules. Walk outdoors only in cooler hours in Makkah/Jeddah heat.
notes: Umbrella target; BODY-02 (walking) and BODY-05 (strength) feed into it. 'Moderate' = can talk but not sing.

what: Walk daily and track steps with the phone or a watch; raise the daily average gradually from her own baseline.
dose: Dose-response evidence (observational): inflection at around 5,000-7,000 steps/day for all-cause mortality, CVD, dementia and falls; 7,000 vs 2,000 steps/day linked to 47% lower all-cause mortality (Ding 2025). In adults <60, mortality risk kept falling up to 8,000-10,000 steps/day (Paluch 2022). No official step target is set.
why: More daily steps are associated with lower risk of death, heart disease and depressive symptoms, with most of the gain reached by about 7,000 steps/day.

sources.title: Daily steps and health outcomes in adults: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
Daily steps and all-cause mortality: a meta-analysis of 15 international cohorts

cue_suggestion: After Maghrib prayer (cooler hours) or right after a phone call - 'walk-and-talk'.
minimum_version: 1,000 extra steps: a 10-min walk around the house/mall corridor.
normal_version: Reach ~7,000 steps/day on most days.
bonus_version: 8,000-10,000 steps via a longer evening walk with a friend/family member.
joy_pairing: Walk-and-talk calls with a friend; audiobook or IELTS listening podcast only while walking (temptation bundle); malls or corniche for scenery.
friction_down: Step widget on home screen; default walking route saved; comfortable shoes by the door.
if_then_plan: If by 8 pm I am under 5,000 steps, then I will do a 15-minute indoor walk while listening to my podcast.
progression: Self-paced: raise 7-day average in small steps from baseline; sources give dose-response, not a ramp rate.
safety_or_stop_rule: Avoid outdoor walking in peak heat; carry water; stop per BODY-25.
notes: 10,000 is not an official threshold; Ding 2025 frames 7,000 as a realistic target. Evidence is observational (association, not proven cause).

what: Stand up and move (walk, stairs, a few squats) during long study/desk sessions.
dose: Saudi PHA: reduce prolonged sitting and break it up as often as possible with at least light activity. WHO: reduce sedentary time (no threshold quantified). In crossover trials, interrupting sitting at least every 30 min lowered glucose more than less frequent breaks (Yin 2024).
why: Replacing sitting with any activity carries health benefits, and frequent breaks improved post-meal glucose in lab trials.

sources.title: Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Practice Guidelines for Saudi Arabia (PDF)
World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
Optimal Frequency of Interrupting Prolonged Sitting for Cardiometabolic Health: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Crossover Trials
ACSM position stand. Quantity and quality of exercise for developing and maintaining cardiorespiratory, musculoskeletal, and neuromotor fitness in apparently healthy adults

cue_suggestion: End of each Pomodoro/study block, or every time a video lesson ends.
minimum_version: Stand and stretch 30 seconds.
normal_version: 2-3 min walk or stairs every ~30 min of sitting.
bonus_version: Take calls and meeting-free reading standing or walking.
joy_pairing: Use the break as a 'song break' - one song, move to it.
friction_down: Timer built into the app's focus sessions; water bottle kept away from the desk so refills force a walk.
if_then_plan: If my focus timer ends, then I will stand and walk until the next song ends.
tracking_metric: Number of breaks taken today (tap per break).
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: Pairs with IELTS/UX study blocks. Sources do not set a daily sitting-hours limit.

what: Insert 1-2 minute bursts of vigorous effort into daily life: fast stairs, brisk uphill walking, fast squats or jumping jacks.
dose: Observational: ~3 bouts/day of 1-2 min vigorous intermittent lifestyle activity was associated with 38-40% lower all-cause mortality in non-exercisers (UK Biobank, mean age ~62). Low-certainty SR: exercise snacks give a small improvement in neuromuscular performance in insufficiently active adults. No official dose.
why: Brief vigorous bursts are associated with lower mortality and can be a starting point for people not doing structured exercise.

sources.title: Association of wearable device-measured vigorous intermittent lifestyle physical activity with mortality
Effects of exercise snacking on neuromuscular performance in insufficiently active adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis

cue_suggestion: Every time she takes the stairs or before sitting down to study.
minimum_version: One 1-minute burst (e.g., fast stair climb).
normal_version: 3 bursts across the day.
bonus_version: Use on rest-from-workout days to keep momentum.
joy_pairing: Treat it as a game: 'beat the song chorus' burst; streak confetti in the app.
friction_down: No equipment, no changing clothes needed.
friction_up_for_competing: Choose stairs over elevator as a default rule.
if_then_plan: If I arrive at a building with stairs, then I will take them fast for the first flights.
safety_or_stop_rule: Vigorous effort: stop per BODY-25 warning signs.
notes: Mortality data come from an older cohort; treat as a supplement to, not replacement for, BODY-01 and BODY-05.

what: Train all major muscle groups (legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders, arms) at home with bodyweight, bands or dumbbells; progress when the current load becomes easy.
dose: At least 2 days/week for all major muscle groups (WHO, CDC, Saudi MOH); ACSM: 2-3 days/week. Observational dose-response: maximum risk reduction at ~30-60 min/week of muscle-strengthening (Momma 2022). Novices: loads around 8-12 repetition maximum, 2-3 days/week; increase load 2-10% when she can do 1-2 reps more than target (ACSM 2009).
why: Muscle-strengthening activity is associated with 10-17% lower risk of all-cause mortality, CVD, cancer and diabetes, independent of aerobic activity.

Saudi Ministry of Health - Physical Activity (health awareness)

cue_suggestion: After Asr prayer on 2-3 of her 4 home-workout days (e.g., Sun/Tue/Thu).
minimum_version: One circuit: squat, push-up (wall/knee), glute bridge, row with band - 1 set each.
normal_version: 20-30 min full-body session, 1-3 sets per exercise, reps in the 8-12 range to near-fatigue.
bonus_version: Add a third weekly session or a harder variation (split squat, elevated push-up).
joy_pairing: Upbeat playlist (BODY-11); 'new move of the week' for novelty; log a PR badge when a harder variation is unlocked.
friction_down: Mat and bands stay out; one saved routine with video demos; no decision needed on the day.
friction_up_for_competing: Workout starts before phone social time after Asr.
if_then_plan: If I can do 2 reps more than my target on an exercise for two sessions, then I will move to the next harder variation or heavier weight.
tracking_metric: Sessions this week (0-3) + top variation/weight per exercise.
progression: ACSM 2009: increase load 2-10% when current load allows 1-2 reps above target. For bodyweight, a harder variation is the home equivalent (adaptation, not stated in source).
safety_or_stop_rule: Controlled form; sharp joint pain = stop that exercise. See BODY-25.
notes: The J-shaped curve (Momma 2022) means >60 min/week showed no extra observed benefit for some outcomes; no need to over-train.

what: Stretch each major muscle-tendon group; end workouts or study days with a short mobility routine.
dose: ACSM 2011: flexibility exercises for each major muscle-tendon group, a total of 60 s per exercise, on at least 2 days/week. Strength training itself also improves joint flexibility (SR, high risk of bias).
why: Flexibility exercise maintains joint range of motion (ACSM).

sources.title: ACSM position stand. Quantity and quality of exercise for developing and maintaining cardiorespiratory, musculoskeletal, and neuromotor fitness in apparently healthy adults
The Influence of Resistance Training on Joint Flexibility in Healthy Adults: A Systematic Review, Meta-analysis, and Meta-regression

cue_suggestion: Immediately after a strength session, or after Isha before wind-down.
minimum_version: 3 stretches x 60 s (hips, hamstrings, chest).
normal_version: 8-10 min covering the major groups, 60 s total each.
bonus_version: Guided mobility/yoga-style video on a rest day.
joy_pairing: Calm playlist, dim warm light - doubles as a wind-down cue (BODY-17).
friction_down: One saved 10-min routine; do it on the same mat.
if_then_plan: If I finish a workout, then I will do my 60-second stretches before showering.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stretch to mild tension, not pain.
notes: 60 s may be split into shorter holds per the ACSM total-time framing.

what: Optional weekly Pilates-based session (online is fine) as an enjoyable variation within the strength/mobility plan.
dose: not specified by source (SR: even once-weekly programs were associated with improvements, but optimal dose unclear).
why: Pilates-based exercise showed benefits for quality of life and self-esteem; evidence for depression/anxiety is limited; remote and in-person delivery performed similarly in adults.

sources.title: Effects of Pilates-Based Exercise on Mental Health, Psychological Well-Being, and Quality of Life: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

cue_suggestion: Weekend morning slot.
minimum_version: 15-min beginner video.
normal_version: 30-45 min class, once a week.
bonus_version: Do it with a friend over video call.
joy_pairing: Try different instructors for novelty; it counts as a 'fun' workout day.
friction_down: Save 3 favourite videos in the app.
if_then_plan: If I feel bored of my strength routine, then I will swap one session for Pilates that week.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stop if back pain worsens; see professional if persistent.
notes: Evidence is heterogeneous (I2 ~92%) and mixes clinical/non-clinical groups; do not claim posture or 'core-fixes-back-pain' benefits from this source.

what: Set up a comfortable laptop/desk arrangement and, more importantly, change position and take brief breaks.
dose: not specified by source. Cochrane: workstation adjustment and sit-stand desks showed no effect on upper-limb pain; supplementary breaks had very-low-quality evidence of reducing neck/shoulder/arm discomfort.
why: Ergonomic equipment alone has weak/inconsistent evidence; breaks have some (very low quality) evidence for less discomfort.

sources.title: Ergonomic interventions for preventing work-related musculoskeletal disorders of the upper limb and neck among office workers

cue_suggestion: Same focus-timer cue as BODY-03.
minimum_version: Change posture and roll shoulders at each timer.
normal_version: Comfortable setup (screen roughly at eye level, feet supported) + BODY-03 breaks.
bonus_version: Laptop stand + external keyboard for long design sessions (comfort choice, not evidence-proven).
joy_pairing: Make the desk a pleasant space (plant, light) she wants to sit at - and leave regularly.
friction_down: One-time setup task in the app.
if_then_plan: If I notice neck or wrist discomfort, then I will stand up and take a 2-minute break immediately.
safety_or_stop_rule: Persistent pain, numbness or tingling: see a physiotherapist/doctor.
notes: Honest framing: no 'perfect posture' evidence found; movement variety is the defensible message. Setup details (eye level etc.) are common practice, not from the cited source.

what: Pick an intensity that feels good during the session (can talk, feels pleasant) and allow herself to adjust it mid-workout.
dose: not specified by source.
why: Feeling better during moderate exercise predicts future activity; in an RCT, pleasure-oriented intensity prescription led to 77% more gym sessions over 8 weeks; allowing intensity adjustment improved affect in young adults.

sources.title: Can the Affective Response to Exercise Predict Future Motives and Physical Activity Behavior? A Systematic Review of Published Evidence
Individualized pleasure-oriented exercise sessions, exercise frequency, and affective outcomes: a pragmatic randomized controlled trial
Making the exercise experience more pleasurable: Exploring the psychological effect of allowing intensity adjustments during exercise

cue_suggestion: Start of every workout: rate 'how do I feel?' on a -5..+5 scale.
minimum_version: Keep the session but lower intensity if the feeling drops below 0.
normal_version: Stay in the zone that feels pleasant most of the time.
bonus_version: Push harder only at the end when feeling good (end on a high).
joy_pairing: End each session with the favourite move/song so the remembered feeling is positive.
friction_down: One-tap feeling rating in the app before/after.
if_then_plan: If the workout starts feeling bad, then I will lower the intensity rather than stop.
safety_or_stop_rule: See BODY-25.
notes: RCT was small (n=47) and short-term; still a strong fit for her goal of linking routines to enjoyment.

what: Listen to music she likes during exercise; faster-tempo tracks for cardio/strength.
dose: not specified by source.
why: Meta-analysis of 139 studies: music improved affective valence, physical performance, and reduced perceived exertion; performance effects larger with fast tempo.

sources.title: Effects of music in exercise and sport: A meta-analytic review

cue_suggestion: Pressing play = workout starts.
minimum_version: One song of movement.
normal_version: Dedicated workout playlist for the whole session.
bonus_version: Build playlists by tempo for warm-up, main set, cool-down.
joy_pairing: Workout-only playlist she looks forward to.
friction_down: Playlist linked from the workout card in the app.
if_then_plan: If I don't feel like exercising, then I will put on my workout playlist and only commit to the first song.
tracking_metric: None needed (optional: favourite track of the week).
safety_or_stop_rule: Keep volume safe; stay aware of surroundings when walking outdoors.
notes: If she prefers not to listen to music, podcasts/audiobooks fit the temptation-bundling action (BODY-11) instead - the music evidence does not cover spoken audio.

what: Reserve a 'want' pleasure (a gripping audiobook, series, podcast) for exercise time only.
dose: not specified by source.
why: In a field experiment, gym-only access to tempting audiobooks increased gym visits by 51% initially, though effects declined over time (especially after a holiday).

sources.title: Holding the Hunger Games Hostage at the Gym: An Evaluation of Temptation Bundling

cue_suggestion: Walking or cardio sessions.
minimum_version: Listen to one chapter while walking.
normal_version: The bundled show/book is only allowed during walks/workouts.
bonus_version: Refresh the bundle monthly with a new story to fight fade-out.
joy_pairing: This IS the joy pairing.
friction_down: Downloaded episodes ready offline.
friction_up_for_competing: Hide the bundled app/series from the home screen outside workout time.
if_then_plan: If I want to hear the next chapter, then I will put on my shoes and walk.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stay alert to traffic if walking outdoors.
notes: Effect decays; plan renewal and a restart after breaks (see BODY-12).

name_en: Comeback reward after a missed workout
what: When a planned workout is missed, make the next session the priority and give a small reward for returning, rather than treating the week as ruined.
dose: not specified by source.
why: In a 61,293-person megastudy, the top intervention offered micro-rewards for returning to the gym after a missed workout; 45% of interventions increased visits but few effects lasted beyond 4 weeks.

sources.title: Megastudies improve the impact of applied behavioural science

cue_suggestion: App detects a missed planned workout.
minimum_version: Next day: 10-minute minimum version earns the comeback badge.
normal_version: Next scheduled session done = comeback reward (points/treat).
bonus_version: Two comebacks in a row unlock something she wants (new playlist, class).
joy_pairing: Visible comeback badge; celebrate returns, not only streaks.
friction_down: Auto-reschedule missed session to the next free slot.
if_then_plan: If I miss a planned workout, then I will do the minimum version at the next Asr and log a comeback.
safety_or_stop_rule: If missed due to illness, rest first (BODY-25).
notes: Design implication for the life-OS: reward recovery, avoid punishing broken streaks. Megastudy population was gym members in the US.

what: Schedule some walks/workouts with a friend, sister, or an online class/group; or set up mutual check-ins.
dose: not specified by source.
why: A Community Guide systematic review found social-support interventions in community settings effective for increasing physical activity.

sources.title: The effectiveness of interventions to increase physical activity. A systematic review
NHS Cheshire and Merseyside - Getting active

cue_suggestion: Fixed weekly walk with a friend (e.g., Thursday evening).
minimum_version: Send a 'done' message to an accountability buddy.
normal_version: One shared walk or class per week.
bonus_version: Join a women's walking group or gym class.
joy_pairing: Combine with social time and a coffee/juice after (caffeine timing per BODY-16).
friction_down: Recurring calendar invite; shared step challenge in a phone app.
if_then_plan: If my buddy cancels, then I will do the walk alone with my bundled podcast.
safety_or_stop_rule: None specific.
notes: Evidence is older (2002) and at community-program level; dropped: family-based social support had inconsistent findings in the same review.

what: Plan the night so there is at least 7 hours of sleep opportunity; set bedtime by counting back from wake time.
dose: Adults: 7 or more hours per night (AASM/SRS; CDC for ages 18-60; Saudi PHA: >=7 h of good sleep, young adults 18-25 aim for 7-9 h).
why: Consensus statements define >=7 h as the amount needed to promote optimal health in adults.

sources.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult: A Joint Consensus Statement of the AASM and SRS
CDC - About Sleep (recommendations and healthy sleep habits)
The recommended amount of physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration for healthy Saudis: A joint consensus statement of the Saudi Public Health Authority
Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Practice Guidelines for Saudi Arabia (PDF)

cue_suggestion: Bedtime alarm = wake time minus 7.5 h (includes time to fall asleep; buffer is a planning choice).
minimum_version: In bed with lights off by planned time on 5 of 7 nights.
normal_version: 7-9 h sleep opportunity nightly.
bonus_version: Weekly review of average sleep in the app.
joy_pairing: Make the pre-bed routine something she enjoys (reading paper book, skincare, Quran recitation).
friction_down: App schedules evening tasks to end before wind-down.
friction_up_for_competing: Phone charges outside bed reach (see BODY-17).
if_then_plan: If my bedtime alarm rings, then I will stop what I'm doing and start my wind-down.
safety_or_stop_rule: Persistent insomnia, loud snoring/breathing pauses, or daytime sleepiness despite enough sleep: see a doctor.
notes: Saudi PHA (conditional): splitting night sleep around Fajr prayer showed no evidence of harm - total sleep is what to protect.

what: Wake up and go to bed at roughly the same time every day, including weekends.
dose: not specified by source (CDC: same time every day; no numeric tolerance given).
why: In a UK Biobank cohort (older adults, observational), higher sleep regularity predicted lower mortality more strongly than sleep duration.

sources.title: CDC - About Sleep (recommendations and healthy sleep habits)
Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Practice Guidelines for Saudi Arabia (PDF)
Sleep regularity is a stronger predictor of mortality risk than sleep duration: A prospective cohort study

cue_suggestion: Anchor wake time to Fajr or a fixed alarm after it.
minimum_version: Same wake time on weekdays; weekend within a small window she chooses.
normal_version: Same wake and bedtime all 7 days.
bonus_version: Morning daylight walk right after waking (BODY-18).
joy_pairing: A morning ritual she looks forward to (favourite drink, sunlight, playlist).
friction_down: One recurring alarm; app day-plan starts at the same time daily.
if_then_plan: If I stayed up late, then I will still wake at my usual time and take a short early-afternoon nap if needed (BODY-20).
tracking_metric: Wake time logged (auto from alarm dismiss).
safety_or_stop_rule: None.
notes: Regularity evidence is observational in older adults; guidelines (CDC, Saudi PHA) still recommend consistency.

what: Set a daily caffeine cutoff time based on bedtime.
dose: Meta-analysis: coffee (~107 mg/250 mL) at least 8.8 h before bedtime; a standard pre-workout supplement (~217.5 mg) at least 13.2 h before bedtime. CDC: avoid caffeine in the afternoon or evening.
why: Caffeine reduced total sleep time by 45 min and sleep efficiency by 7% on average.

sources.title: The effect of caffeine on subsequent sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis
CDC - About Sleep (recommendations and healthy sleep habits)

cue_suggestion: App shows 'last coffee' time computed from bedtime (e.g., bed 23:00 -> coffee before ~14:10).
minimum_version: No caffeine after Asr.
normal_version: Last coffee/tea/energy drink before the computed cutoff.
bonus_version: Switch afternoon drink to decaf or herbal.
joy_pairing: Keep a pleasant non-caffeinated afternoon drink ritual (karak-style decaf, herbal tea).
friction_down: Stock decaf/herbal options.
friction_up_for_competing: Don't keep energy drinks at home.
if_then_plan: If I want coffee after the cutoff, then I will have my decaf/herbal drink instead.
safety_or_stop_rule: None.
notes: Arabic coffee and tea also contain caffeine; source doses are for coffee and pre-workout supplements specifically.

name_en: Evening wind-down: dim light, devices off
name_ar: روتين التهدئة المسائي: إضاءة خافتة وإبعاد الأجهزة
what: Dim home lighting in the evening, stop screens before bed, and switch to a non-screen activity.
dose: CDC: turn off electronic devices at least 30 min before bedtime. Expert consensus: from at least 3 h before bedtime keep light at the eye <=10 lux melanopic EDI; sleep environment as dark as possible (<=1 lux).
why: Reading on a light-emitting device before bed delayed sleep onset, suppressed melatonin, shifted the body clock and reduced next-morning alertness vs a printed book (small RCT).

sources.title: CDC - About Sleep (recommendations and healthy sleep habits)
Recommendations for daytime, evening, and nighttime indoor light exposure to best support physiology, sleep, and wakefulness in healthy adults
Brown et al. 2022 full text (light recommendations)
Evening use of light-emitting eReaders negatively affects sleep, circadian timing, and next-morning alertness

cue_suggestion: After Isha prayer: switch to warm/dim lamps.
minimum_version: Phone away 30 min before bed.
normal_version: Dim lights ~3 h before bed; last 30-60 min screen-free (paper book, stretching, journaling).
bonus_version: Phone charges outside the bedroom.
joy_pairing: A paper novel or English (IELTS) reader she enjoys only in bed; calm stretching (BODY-06).
friction_down: Smart-home/phone schedule for dim lights and Do Not Disturb.
friction_up_for_competing: App limits on social/video apps after wind-down start.
if_then_plan: If I catch myself scrolling after my wind-down time, then I will put the phone on the charger outside my room.
safety_or_stop_rule: None.
notes: Melanopic EDI is a lab/lighting metric; practical translation = dim, warm lighting. The eReader RCT was small (n=12).

what: Get bright light during the day, ideally daylight (e.g., sit by a window while studying, short outdoor time in cooler early hours).
dose: Expert consensus: daytime minimum melanopic EDI of 250 lux at the eye; use daylight first where available. No minutes-per-day dose stated.
why: Consensus recommends bright daytime light to support circadian rhythm, sleep and alertness.

sources.title: Recommendations for daytime, evening, and nighttime indoor light exposure to best support physiology, sleep, and wakefulness in healthy adults
Brown et al. 2022 full text (light recommendations)

cue_suggestion: Right after Fajr/waking: open curtains; study near a window.
minimum_version: Open curtains and have breakfast by the window.
normal_version: Study/work in a daylit spot; brief outdoor time in cool early morning.
bonus_version: Morning walk outdoors when temperature allows (combine with BODY-02).
joy_pairing: Morning coffee on a balcony (within caffeine window).
friction_down: Move desk near a window (one-time project step).
if_then_plan: If I start a study session, then I will sit in the brightest daylit spot available.
safety_or_stop_rule: Avoid midday heat; never look at the sun.
notes: Source addresses daytime generally, not specifically 'morning within X minutes' - avoid claiming a morning-light dose.

what: Decide a 'go to bed' time and pre-commit with a plan for the usual delay trigger (scrolling, series, late work).
dose: not specified by source.
why: In a representative Dutch sample, going to bed later than intended without external reasons (bedtime procrastination) mediated the link between low self-regulation and insufficient sleep.

sources.title: Bedtime procrastination: A self-regulation perspective on sleep insufficiency in the general population

cue_suggestion: Wind-down alarm (BODY-17).
minimum_version: Name the delay trigger tonight and set the phone to charge outside the room.
normal_version: Use if-then plan nightly; review weekly which trigger won.
bonus_version: Move 'revenge' leisure (series) to earlier evening as a planned reward.
joy_pairing: Schedule guilt-free leisure earlier so bedtime doesn't feel like losing 'me time'.
friction_down: Auto Do Not Disturb + app lock at wind-down.
friction_up_for_competing: Log out of the most tempting app at night; disable autoplay.
if_then_plan: If one episode ends after my wind-down time, then I will close the app and not start the next.
safety_or_stop_rule: None.
notes: The intervention side (if-then plans) is general behavior science, not tested in this source.

what: If sleepy, take a short nap around midday; keep it short.
dose: Saudi PHA: napping around midday (noontime) is acceptable, limited to less than 30 min. Cohort meta-analysis: naps >=30 min associated with higher mortality/CVD/metabolic risk; <30 min not. Lab meta-analysis: naps improved alertness, with early-afternoon naps (before 13:00) better.
why: Short naps improved cognitive performance (especially alertness) in lab studies, while long habitual naps were associated with higher health risks.

sources.title: Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Practice Guidelines for Saudi Arabia (PDF)
To nap or not? Evidence from a meta-analysis of cohort studies of habitual daytime napping and health outcomes
Effects of a Short Daytime Nap on the Cognitive Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

cue_suggestion: After Dhuhr prayer, only when needed.
minimum_version: Eyes-closed rest 10 min.
normal_version: Nap under 30 min with an alarm.
bonus_version: n/a
joy_pairing: Quiet, cool, dark spot; calm audio.
friction_down: One-tap 25-min nap timer in the app.
friction_up_for_competing: Alarm across the room to prevent oversleeping.
if_then_plan: If I feel very sleepy after Dhuhr, then I will set a 25-minute alarm and nap.
safety_or_stop_rule: Avoid naps if they make it hard to sleep at night. Needing naps daily despite 7+ h sleep: see a doctor.
notes: Cohort risks are associations, mean age ~56; the Saudi guideline is the most relevant anchor for her.

what: Keep the bedroom quiet, cool and dark; avoid large meals before bedtime.
dose: CDC: bedroom quiet, relaxing, cool temperature; avoid large meals before bedtime. Consensus: sleep environment as dark as possible (<=1 lux melanopic EDI). No specific temperature stated.
why: Individual sleep hygiene components are associated with better sleep, though bundled 'sleep hygiene education' is largely untested in the general population.

sources.title: CDC - About Sleep (recommendations and healthy sleep habits)
Brown et al. 2022 full text (light recommendations)
The role of sleep hygiene in promoting public health: A review of empirical evidence

cue_suggestion: One-time setup + weekly check on the weekend.
minimum_version: Cover LED lights; eye mask.
normal_version: Blackout curtains, AC set cool, quiet (earplugs/white noise if needed), dinner not right before bed.
bonus_version: Remove TV/desk work from bed.
joy_pairing: Make the bed space inviting (fresh sheets, favourite scent).
friction_down: Buy once: blackout curtain, eye mask.

what: During Ramadan, plan a split sleep: a main night block plus a daytime sleep to keep total sleep adequate.
dose: Saudi PHA (as extracted from guideline PDF): sufficient sleep of 4-6 h at night supplemented by 1.5-2 h daytime sleep.
why: Saudi consensus recognizes Ramadan's changed schedule and recommends maintaining adequate total sleep.

what: Drink fluids regularly; drink more in heat and when active.
dose: NHS: aim for 6-8 cups or glasses of fluid a day (water, lower-fat milk, sugar-free drinks including tea and coffee count); more if in a hot environment or physically active for long periods. EFSA: 2.0 L/day considered adequate for women (total water intake).
why: Official bodies set adequate intakes; needs rise in hot environments and with prolonged activity.

what: Be aware vitamin D deficiency is common in Saudi Arabia; if concerned, ask a doctor whether testing/supplementation is appropriate. Sun exposure can help but no safe minutes-dose is sourced.
dose: not specified by source (Saudi expert consensus: universal screening not recommended; correction advised if serum 25(OH)D <50 nmol/L; a Riyadh lab study identified best sun windows for previtamin D3 production: summer ~09:00-10:30 and 14:00-15:00, winter 10:00-14:00).
why: Saudi experts note deficiency is common; sunlight drives vitamin D production, with time of day mattering.

what: Keep lighter/rest days between hard sessions and know when to stop exercise and seek help (chest pain, dizziness, feeling very unwell, heat illness signs).
dose: Rest-day number: not specified by source. Stop and seek medical advice for chest pain, dizziness or feeling very unwell (NHS). Heat stroke (confusion, slurred speech, very high body temperature): emergency; heat exhaustion (headache, nausea, dizziness, weakness, heavy sweating): leave the heat, drink, cool down (CDC NIOSH).
why: Exercise is safe for most people, and exercise-related cardiac events are often preceded by warning signs/symptoms (ACSM).

cue_suggestion: Weekly plan: alternate strength days; walking/mobility on off days. Stop card shown on every workout screen.
minimum_version: Full rest day when sick or very fatigued.
normal_version: 1-3 non-strength days/week with easy walking or mobility.
bonus_version: Weekly check: sleep, soreness, mood - lighten the week if all low.
joy_pairing: Rest days = enjoyable easy movement (social walk, Pilates).
friction_down: App auto-plans rest days so rest is 'on plan', not a failure.
if_then_plan: If I feel chest pain, dizziness or very unwell during exercise, then I will stop immediately and seek medical advice.
safety_or_stop_rule: Stop immediately: chest pain/pressure, dizziness/fainting, feeling very unwell, confusion in heat. Emergency care for heat stroke signs. See a doctor before starting vigorous exercise if she has known heart/metabolic/kidney disease or symptoms (ACSM screening logic).
notes: Outdoor heat in Makkah/Jeddah makes heat-illness rules especially relevant. No source found that fixes a rest-day count for general adults.
